helpers.name: reserve_file

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: File path relative to project root

parameters.name: skip_id_naming
parameters.description: If true, skip ID embedding in name (for __init__.py, .db files, MCP tools, or user preference). Sets id_in_name=0 in database.

helpers.purpose: Reserve a file ID before writing code — part of the mandatory reserve-write-finalize tracking flow. Returns ID to embed in filename.
helpers.error_handling: Return error if path already exists
return_statements: Use returned ID for file naming: {name}_id_{id}.{ext}

IMPORTANT: Plan ALL reservations for this file — all public functions MUST be reserved via reserve_function/reserve_functions AND all exported types MUST be reserved via reserve_type/reserve_types BEFORE writing code. File tracking without function+type tracking is incomplete.

MANDATORY FIELDS: When reserving functions, include purpose, parameters, and returns. When reserving types, include definition_json and description. These fields are the AI's primary lookup mechanism across sessions — null fields make entities invisible to future discovery.
After finalization, link this file to flow(s) via add_file_to_flow(file_id, flow_id). Use get_all_flows() or get_task_flows(task_id) to identify the correct flow(s).
Next: write file to disk with ID in name → finalize_file(file_id, name, path, language)

used_by_directives.description: Reserve file ID before writing code - AI embeds ID in filename for instant lookups (filename_id_42.py)
Reserve file ID before generating file content - enables rename-proof references

implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, id: reserved_id, is_reserved: true, id_in_name: !skip_id_naming}
SQL: INSERT INTO files (name, path, language, is_reserved, id_in_name) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 1, ?) RETURNING id
Filename pattern: {name}_id_{id}.{extension} (e.g., calculator_id_42.py) unless skip_id_naming=true
If skip_id_naming=true: id_in_name=0, name stays as-is (for __init__.py, .db files, MCP tools)

helpers.name: reserve_files

parameters.name: files
parameters.description: Array of file objects [{name, path, language, skip_id_naming?}, ...]

helpers.purpose: Batch-reserve file IDs before writing multiple files. Returns IDs in input order for embedding in filenames.
helpers.error_handling: Return error if any path already exists
return_statements: Use returned IDs for file naming: {name}_id_{id}.{ext}

IMPORTANT: Plan ALL reservations for ALL files — all public functions MUST be reserved via reserve_functions AND all exported types MUST be reserved via reserve_types BEFORE writing code. File tracking without function+type tracking is incomplete.

MANDATORY FIELDS: When reserving functions, include purpose, parameters, and returns. When reserving types, include definition_json and description. These fields are the AI's primary lookup mechanism across sessions — null fields make entities invisible to future discovery.
After finalization, link all files to flow(s) via add_file_flows([(file_id, flow_id), ...]). Use get_all_flows() or get_task_flows(task_id) to identify the correct flow(s).
Next: write files to disk with IDs in names → finalize_files([{file_id, name, path, language}, ...])
implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, ids: [id1, id2, ...]} in same order as input files array
SQL: Multiple INSERT INTO files (name, path, language, is_reserved, id_in_name) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 1, ?) (in transaction)
IDs correspond to files array indices: files[0] gets ids[0], files[1] gets ids[1], etc.
Each item has its own skip_id_naming flag - allows mixed batch with some files having IDs, some not
id_in_name is set to !skip_id_naming for each file individually

helpers.name: finalize_file

parameters.name: skip_id_naming
parameters.description: If true, skip _id_XX pattern validation (for files where ID naming was skipped during reservation)

helpers.purpose: Mark a reserved file as tracked after writing it to disk. Triggers flow assignment and function/type tracking checks.
helpers.error_handling: Return error if file doesn't exist at path
return_statements: BLOCKED: Do NOT proceed until all public functions AND all exported types in this file are reserved and finalized. Functions via reserve_function/finalize_function WITH complete fields (purpose, parameters, returns). Types via reserve_type/finalize_type WITH complete fields (definition_json, description). A finalized file with 0 tracked functions or untracked types is incomplete (unless data-only or config-only).

BLOCKED: Link this file to its flow(s) via add_file_to_flow(file_id, flow_id) or add_file_flows([(file_id, flow_id), ...]). A finalized file with 0 flow assignments is architecturally disconnected. Use get_all_flows() or get_task_flows(task_id) to identify the correct flow(s).

MODULE CHECK: If this file contains domain logic or wraps external dependencies, assign it to a module via add_file_to_module(file_id, module_id). Use get_module_for_file(file_id) to check if already assigned, search_modules() to find the right module, or add_module() to create one. Orchestrator files (pages, handlers, commands) do NOT need module assignment.
If called during project_reserve_finalize: follow project_update_db directive to sync reserved IDs with database.
After file write operations: route to git_sync_state directive to update last_known_git_hash
Call aimfp_run(is_new_session=false) — returns watchdog info about external file changes detected since your last check.

used_by_directives.description: Finalize file after code written - sets is_reserved=false and confirms file exists on filesystem
Finalize file reservation after successful file generation
Finalize file reservations when updating database with new file metadata

implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, file_id: file_id}
Verifies file exists at path using os.path.exists()
SQL: UPDATE files SET is_reserved=0, name=?, path=?, language=? WHERE id=?
Name validation: must contain '_id_{file_id}' pattern UNLESS skip_id_naming=true
If skip_id_naming=true: skip _id_XX validation, file was reserved with id_in_name=0
Note: File change tracking uses Git, not database checksums

helpers.name: finalize_files

parameters.name: files
parameters.description: Array of file objects [{file_id, name, path, language, skip_id_naming?}, ...]

helpers.purpose: Batch-finalize multiple reserved files after writing them to disk. All-or-nothing operation.
helpers.error_handling: Return error if any file doesn't exist at path
return_statements: BLOCKED: Do NOT proceed until all public functions AND all exported types in ALL finalized files are reserved and finalized. Functions via reserve_functions/finalize_functions WITH complete fields (purpose, parameters, returns). Types via reserve_types/finalize_types WITH complete fields (definition_json, description). Finalized files with 0 tracked functions or untracked types are incomplete (unless data-only or config-only).

BLOCKED: Link ALL finalized files to their flow(s) via add_file_to_flow(file_id, flow_id) or add_file_flows([(file_id, flow_id), ...]). Finalized files with 0 flow assignments are architecturally disconnected. Use get_all_flows() or get_task_flows(task_id) to identify the correct flow(s).

MODULE CHECK: For each finalized file containing domain logic or external dependency wrappers, assign to a module via add_file_to_module(file_id, module_id). Use search_modules() to find the right module or add_module() to create one. Orchestrator files (pages, handlers, commands) do NOT need module assignment.
If called during project_reserve_finalize: follow project_update_db directive to sync reserved IDs with database.
After file write operations: route to git_sync_state directive to update last_known_git_hash
Call aimfp_run(is_new_session=false) — returns watchdog info about external file changes detected since your last check.
implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, finalized_ids: [...]} confirming which IDs were finalized
Verifies each file exists on filesystem
SQL: Multiple UPDATE files SET is_reserved=0, name=?, path=?, language=? WHERE id=? (in transaction)
All operations succeed or all fail - no partial finalization
Each item has its own skip_id_naming flag - validation is per-item, not global
If skip_id_naming=true for an item, skip _id_XX pattern validation for that specific file
Note: File change tracking uses Git, not database checksums

helpers.name: get_file_by_name
helpers.purpose: Look up a tracked file by name — use BEFORE reading source files. Returns metadata, path, and ID for follow-up queries.
helpers.error_handling: Return error if no files found with that name
return_statements: File names are not unique — if several files match, pick by path. No match for a file that exists on disk means it is untracked: catalog_files (existing code) or reserve_file (new file).

used_by_directives.description: Look up files by name during DB-filesystem sync - verifies file entries exist before syncing dependencies
Query files by name for dependency graph generation - maps relationships between files, functions, and flows

implementation_notes: Returns array of file objects (multiple files can share same name, e.g. __init__.py)
SQL: SELECT * FROM files WHERE name=?
Returns: {success, files: [{id, name, path, language, is_reserved, id_in_name, created_at, updated_at}, ...]}
Returns FilesQueryResult (not FileQueryResult) — uses files tuple, not single file

helpers.name: get_file_by_path
helpers.purpose: Look up a tracked file by path — use BEFORE reading source files. Returns file metadata and ID for follow-up queries.
return_statements: file is null for a path that exists on disk → the file is untracked: catalog_files (existing code) or reserve_file (new file).

used_by_directives.description: Load file metadata from database by path - provides full context including functions, dependencies, theme/flow associations
Check if file exists in database before deletion - ensures proper cleanup of DB records
Look up files by path during DB-filesystem sync - verifies file entries exist before syncing dependencies
Query files by path for dependency graph generation - maps relationships between files, functions, and flows
Validate file paths exist in database during integrity checks - detects missing or orphaned file records

implementation_notes: Returns file object or null if not found
SQL: SELECT * FROM files WHERE path=? LIMIT 1
Returns: {id, name, path, language, is_reserved, created_at, updated_at}

helpers.name: update_file
helpers.error_handling: Return error if file_id not found
return_statements: Ensure name or path changes are updated throughout codebase
If name changed, verify _id_xxx suffix is retained
If file path or purpose changed, verify file_flows entries are still correct

used_by_directives.description: Update file metadata after code generation - synchronizes file information
Update stale file metadata during DB-filesystem sync - refreshes file information
Verify file metadata during integrity validation - ensures database matches filesystem

implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, file_id: file_id}
SQL: UPDATE files SET name=?, path=?, language=?, updated_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id=?
Only updates non-NULL parameters - partial updates supported
Note: File change tracking uses Git, not database fields

helpers.name: file_has_changed
helpers.purpose: Check if file changed using Git (if available) or filesystem timestamp
helpers.error_handling: Return error if file_id not found

used_by_directives.description: Detect if file changed since last DB update - warns user about potential staleness
Check if files changed during integrity validation - detects checksum mismatches that need correction
Detect which files changed during DB-filesystem sync - identifies stale entries that need re-syncing

implementation_notes: Returns {changed: boolean, method: 'git'|'filesystem'}
Git method: git diff --quiet <path> (if git available)
Filesystem method: Compare file's last modified timestamp with updated_at in database
Prefers git method if available, falls back to filesystem timestamp comparison

helpers.name: update_file_timestamp

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: File ID to update timestamp for

helpers.purpose: Update file timestamp (called automatically after function updates)
helpers.error_handling: Return error if file_id not found
implementation_notes: Returns {success: true}
Sub-helper: not exposed as MCP tool, only called internally
Updates timestamp to mark file as recently modified
SQL: UPDATE files SET updated_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id=?

helpers.name: delete_file
helpers.purpose: Delete file with comprehensive cross-reference validation
helpers.error_handling: Return error if functions/types exist for file - requires manual cleanup. File_flows are auto-cleared when no other dependencies remain.
return_statements: Ensure the file is also deleted from the filesystem, not just the database

used_by_directives.description: Delete file from filesystem and database with cascade cleanup of functions and interactions

implementation_notes: ERROR LOGIC: Query files table for is_reserved WHERE id=? - if is_reserved=1, return error
ERROR RETURN (reserved): {success: false, error: "file_reserved", message: "Cannot delete reserved file. Use delete_reserved helper to clean up abandoned reservation"}
ERROR LOGIC: Query functions table WHERE file_id=? - if not empty, return error with dependency list
ERROR LOGIC: Query types table WHERE file_id=? - if not empty, return error with dependency list
ERROR RETURN (functions/types): {success: false, error: "dependencies_exist", dependencies: {functions: [...], types: [...], file_flows: [...]}}
AUTO-CLEAR: If functions and types are empty but file_flows exist, auto-delete all file_flows entries for the file
SUCCESS LOGIC: Create note entry in notes table with reason, severity, source, type, reference details
SUCCESS LOGIC: Delete file entry: DELETE FROM files WHERE id=file_id
SUCCESS RETURN: {success: true, deleted_file_id: file_id, cleared_file_flows: [...flow_names]}
RETURN STATEMENT: When file_flows were auto-cleared, appends guidance to verify flow coverage
NOTE: Functions and types have SQL ON DELETE CASCADE to files, but we prevent this by checking dependencies first
